Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testOptionComparatorInsertedOrder()` verifies that the options returned from `getOptions().getOptions()` are in the inserted order matching `insertedOrder`. The `getOptions()` method in the test returns an `Options` object configured with various options and option groups.

The key point is how `Options.getOptions()` returns the collection of options. It calls `helpOptions()`, which returns a new `ArrayList` from `shortOpts.values()`. The `shortOpts` map is a `LinkedHashMap` as the field declaration shows, which preserves insertion order when options are added via `Options.addOption(Option)`.

In `Options.addOption(Option)`, every new option is added to `shortOpts` via a `put` call. Since `shortOpts` is a `LinkedHashMap`, the insertion order is preserved in its `values()` view. Consequently, `getOptions()` returns options in insertion order unless a comparator alters the order.

The current bug report states that calling `HelpFormatter.setOptionComparator(null)` does not display options in inserted order. The root cause is that setting the comparator to `null` in `HelpFormatter` does not correctly reset the comparator to preserve natural or insertion order, or the `HelpFormatter` part that sorts options does not handle a `null` comparator case properly. The test's expected behavior matches options in insertion order, so the discrepancy lies in how `HelpFormatter` uses the comparator to sort options for display.

Therefore, the bug arises because `HelpFormatter`'s handling of `optionComparator` when set to `null` doesn't default back to insertion order sorting of options, leading to options not displayed in the inserted order.

No recent bug reports were available for additional clues, so the analysis relied on the test, current bug report, and relevant code snippets from `Options` and `HelpFormatter`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
